14: # SKILL.md File Templates - Creation Guide
15: 
16: Templates for creating SKILL.md files with proper structure, frontmatter, and required sections.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines for SKILL.md (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)
68: 
69: **Quality Targets**:
70: - Structure: 100/100
71: - Content quality: High (AI-evaluated)
72: - Overall: High (human/AI judgment)
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## 2. FRONTMATTER REQUIREMENTS
77: 
78: ### Required Fields
79: 
80: | Field | Required | Format | Example |
81: |-------|----------|--------|---------|
82: | `name` | ✅ | hyphen-case | `my-skill-name` |
83: | `description` | ✅ | Single line, **≤ 130 chars** for skills (≤ 110 for commands), 1,536-char hard cap | `"Handles X when Y occurs"` |
84: | `allowed-tools` | ✅ | Array: `[Tool1, Tool2]` | `[Read, Write, Edit, Bash]` |
85: | `version` | ✅ | 4-part X.Y.Z.W | `1.0.0.0` |
86: 
87: > **Hard rules**: not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside the skill's `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects that the dispatch preflight reads.
88: 
89: > **Description budget & trim style**: see [`frontmatter-templates.md` § Description Budget & Trim Style](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md).
90: > Keep total project descriptions under the ~6,400-character ceiling. This leaves headroom below the 8,000-character auto-discovery limit.
91: > Drop product and stack lists. Drop marketing prose. Keep the skill name, primary verb, domain noun and mode suffixes (`:auto` or `:confirm`).
92: 
93: ### Template
94: 
95: ```yaml
96: ---
97: name: sk-example
98: description: Example workflow skill demonstrating proper frontmatter format with specific capabilities, use cases, and key differentiators for AI agent discovery.
99: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
100: version: 1.0.0.0
101: ---
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Key Rules
105: 
106: - **name**: Must match folder name exactly, hyphen-case only
107: - **description**: Third-person voice, single line, no `<>` brackets
108: - **allowed-tools**: Use brackets `[...]`, not comma-separated string
109: - **hard rules**: Not a frontmatter key. They live in `hard-rules.json` beside `SKILL.md`, a JSON array of `{id, check, message, severity}` objects the dispatch preflight reads.
110: 
111: > **Complete Reference**: For validation rules, edge cases, array formats, and all document type frontmatter, see [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md)
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. SKILL TEMPLATE (WITH BUNDLED RESOURCES)
116: 
117: **Use for**: Skills with bundled resources (references, scripts, or assets)
118: 
119: **Target**: 800-2000 lines (SKILL.md <1000 lines, rest in resources)
120: 
121: **Size Constraints** (package_skill.py validation):
122: - Max 5000 words (3000 recommended)
123: - Max 3000 lines
124:

126: 
127: Packaging enforcement note:
128: - `package_skill.py` fails if `REFERENCES` is missing and no approved combined `SMART ROUTING & REFERENCES` structure exists.
129: 
130: **Recommended Sections**: SUCCESS CRITERIA, INTEGRATION POINTS, REFERENCES AND RELATED RESOURCES
131: 
132: ### Template
133:

135: ---
136: name: example-skill
137: description: Example skill demonstrating proper template structure with specific capabilities for semantic code search and context preservation workflows.
138: allowed-tools: [Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep]
139: version: 1.0.0.0
140: ---
141: ```

14: # README Template and Selection Guide
15: 
16: Use this template for project, skill, feature and component READMEs. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) for source-folder READMEs that explain package topology, files, boundaries and data or control flow.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. README SELECTION
21: 
22: README files answer two questions: what is this, and how does someone use or navigate it?
23: 
24: | Type | Use When | Template |
25: |---|---|---|
26: | Project | The repository or package needs a public entry point | This file |
27: | Skill | A skill needs human-facing context beyond `SKILL.md` | This file |
28: | Feature | A user-facing feature needs setup, usage or behavior notes | This file |
29: | Component | A reusable module has an API, examples or configuration | This file, trimmed |
30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text
35: Is this a project, package, skill or feature root?
36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?
38:     +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
39:     `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
40: ```
41: 
42: Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE
47: 
48: Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.
49: 
50: | Section | Include When | Content |
51: |---|---|---|
52: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
54: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
55: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
56: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
57: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
58: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
59: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
60: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
61: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
62: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
63: | Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |
64: 
65: Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE
70: 
71: Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.
72: 
73: | Profile Block | Good For | Keep It Short By |
74: |---|---|---|
75: | `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
76: | Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
77: | How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
78: | Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
79: | Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |
80: | Related Skills | Skill graph navigation | Group by relationship type |
81: | Related Documents | Operator or developer references | Link stable docs, not packet history |
82: | FAQ | Repeated questions | 3-6 high-value Q&A pairs |
83: 
84: Sections use plain numbered H2 headings. Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments or a Table of Contents.
85: 
86: ```markdown
87: ## 1. OVERVIEW
88: 
89: [Section content]
90: 
91: ```
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. WRITING RULES
96: 
97: Write for scanning first.
98: 
99: - Lead with what the thing does.
100: - Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
101: - Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
102: - Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
103: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
104: - Test commands before documenting them.
105: - Show expected output for verification commands.
106: - Use relative links for local docs.
107: - Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.
108: 
109: The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:
110: 
111: ```markdown
112: **`spec.md`**
113: - What the feature is and why it exists.
114: - Required at every level.
115: ```
116: 
117: Group related items under an unnumbered `#####` heading when the inventory has natural groups, for example by how each item is triggered.
118: 
119: Voice by README type:
120: 
121: | Type | Voice |
122: |---|---|
123: | Project, Skill, Feature | Plain explanation first, reference detail later |
124: | Component | Technical and concise |
125: | Code Folder | Technical and concise, via `readme-code-template.md` |
126: 
127: Human Voice Rules apply to all README content:
128: 
129: - No em dashes. Use commas, periods or colons.
130: - No semicolons. Split the sentence or use "and".
131: - No Oxford comma in inline lists.
132: - No setup phrases.
133: - No banned words from the HVR reference.
134: - Prefer active voice and direct verbs.

138: ---

141: 
142: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.

30: | Code Folder | A source directory needs developer orientation | [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md) |
31: 
32: Create a README when someone can land in the folder and need orientation. Skip it when inline comments or a nearby parent README already explain the folder.
33: 
34: ```text

36: +-- Yes: write a general README.
37: `-- No: is this source-code orientation?
38:     +-- Yes: use readme_code_template.md.
39:     `-- No: write a focused README only if readers need setup, usage or navigation help.
40: ```
41: 
42: Keep READMEs current-state only. Do not cite spec packet numbers, phase IDs or migration history. Use feature names, file paths, commands and stable source links.
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. GENERAL STRUCTURE
47: 
48: Use only the sections that fit the audience. Project and skill READMEs often need most sections. Feature and component READMEs should stay shorter.
49: 
50: | Section | Include When | Content |
51: |---|---|---|
52: | Overview | Always | Purpose, audience, main value and prerequisites |
53: | Key Statistics | Useful facts help readers decide scope | Counts, version, supported modes, limits |
54: | How This Compares | Readers may confuse this with nearby tools | Short comparison table |
55: | Quick Start | Readers need to run or try something | Short setup, verification and first use |
56: | Features | Capabilities need explanation | Feature groups, behavior notes and examples |
57: | Requirements | Runtime, tool or service needs exist | Minimum versions, permissions and external services |
58: | Structure | Navigation matters | Directory tree and key files |
59: | Configuration | Settings exist | Config files, options, defaults and env vars |
60: | Usage Examples | Patterns are easier shown than described | Simple and advanced examples with expected results |
61: | Troubleshooting | Users can hit known issues | What they see, cause and fix |
62: | FAQ | Repeated questions exist | Short answers only |
63: | Related Resources | Always when links exist | Grouped skills, documents, commands or external references |
64: 
65: Code-folder READMEs are different. Do not force Quick Start, Features, FAQ or Troubleshooting unless the directory has runnable commands or known reader problems. Use [`readme-code-template.md`](./readme-code-template.md).
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. SKILL AND PROJECT PROFILE
70: 
71: Use this profile for OpenCode skills, package roots and project-level READMEs that need more than a bare overview.
72: 
73: | Profile Block | Good For | Keep It Short By |
74: |---|---|---|
75: | `trigger_phrases` | Search, memory and skill routing | 3-8 concrete phrases |
76: | Key Statistics | Skill counts, tool counts, version facts | Use one compact table |
77: | How This Compares | Neighboring skills or tools | Compare only reader-relevant differences |
78: | Key Features | Current capability inventory | Group related features |
79: | Requirements | Tooling and runtime needs | Separate required from optional |
80: | Related Skills | Skill graph navigation | Group by relationship type |
81: | Related Documents | Operator or developer references | Link stable docs, not packet history |
82: | FAQ | Repeated questions | 3-6 high-value Q&A pairs |
83: 
84: Sections use plain numbered H2 headings. Do not add `<!-- ANCHOR -->` comments or a Table of Contents.
85: 
86: ```markdown
87: ## 1. OVERVIEW
88: 
89: [Section content]
90: 
91: ```
92: 
93: ---
94: 
95: ## 4. WRITING RULES
96: 
97: Write for scanning first.
98: 
99: - Lead with what the thing does.
100: - Put the fastest useful path before detailed reference.
101: - Use tables for options, file lists and comparisons.
102: - Give every inventory item a description. When an item needs more than one line, switch to the itemized pattern below instead of widening the table.
103: - Use fenced code blocks with language tags.
104: - Test commands before documenting them.
105: - Show expected output for verification commands.
106: - Use relative links for local docs.
107: - Remove unused sections instead of leaving placeholders.
108: 
109: The itemized pattern for inventories where each item needs more than one line:

113: - What the feature is and why it exists.

138: ---
139: 
140: ## 5. FRONTMATTER
141: 
142: Frontmatter is optional for normal project READMEs and recommended for skill or system documentation that should be discoverable.

14: # Skill Authoring Checklist
15: 
16: Checklist for authoring or modifying OpenCode skills with correct metadata, resource layout, parent-hub routing files, versioning, and validation.
17: 
18: ## 1. OVERVIEW
19: 
20: ### Purpose
21: 
22: This checklist keeps new and modified OpenCode skills consistent with the live skill contract. Use it to verify whether the skill is a flat skill or a parent-hub skill, then check metadata, resource layout, routing files, versioning, and validation before handing the skill to another runtime or authoring command.
23: 
24: ### Usage
25: 
26: - Use this when authoring a new skill under `.skilled/skills/`.
27: - Use this when modifying an existing skill's frontmatter, `SKILL.md` structure, allowed tools, bundled references, assets, or scripts.
28: - Use this when promoting a skill from a local draft into the shared OpenCode skill inventory.
29: - Use this when a skill changes routing behavior, resource discovery, or version metadata.
30: - Use this when converting a flat skill into a parent-hub skill with nested mode packets.
31: 
32: ---
33: 
34: ## 2. PRE-CHECKS
35: 
36: - [ ] Read the live parent-hub example at `.skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md`, `.skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md`, `.skilled/skills/sk-code/graph-metadata.json`, `.skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json`, and `.skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json` before copying a hub pattern.
37: - [ ] Read `sk-doc` source rules at `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/README.md` and the parent-hub pattern at `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md`.
38: - [ ] Decide the skill shape: flat skill or parent-hub skill. A parent hub has one advisor-routable identity and nested mode packets.
39: - [ ] For any parent hub, require hub-level `graph-metadata.json`, `mode-registry.json`, `hub-router.json`, and `description.json`; nested packets must not carry their own `graph-metadata.json`.
40: - [ ] Verify whether the target skill uses a 3-part version or a 4-part version; `.skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md` uses a 4-part version.
41: - [ ] Confirm skill frontmatter `allowed-tools` is explicit and no broader than the workflow needs.
42: - [ ] Keep the frontmatter description to 1-2 sentences that explain when the skill should activate.
43: - [ ] Verify bundled `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/` are separated by purpose, not convenience.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## 3. STEPS
48: 
49: 1. Define the skill's activation boundary before drafting content.
50: 2. Choose the shape.
51:    - Flat skill: one `SKILL.md` plus optional `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, and `description.json`.
52:    - Parent-hub skill: hub `SKILL.md`, `ROUTER.md`, `description.json`, `graph-metadata.json`, `mode-registry.json`, `hub-router.json`, and nested packet folders.
53: 3. Create or update `SKILL.md` with required frontmatter, a focused description, and the standard sections used by the live example.
54: 4. For parent hubs, keep stage-one routing in `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json`, and each packet's machine router in that packet's own `ROUTER.md`; keep workflow or surface detail inside nested packet `SKILL.md` files.
55: 5. For parent hubs, keep a single advisor identity in hub-level `graph-metadata.json`; do not add packet-level graph metadata.
56: 6. Put detailed standards in `references/`, reusable output material in `assets/`, and deterministic helpers in `scripts/`.
57: 7. Put the `INTENT_SIGNALS` / `RESOURCE_MAP` block and its routing prose in the packet's own `ROUTER.md`, under a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` heading; a hub root `ROUTER.md` carries the hub's stage-two control document instead. `SKILL.md` SMART ROUTING stays short prose plus the link to that file.
58: 8. Add or update `description.json` with matching version, keywords, and trigger examples.
59: 9. Add changelog coverage when the skill has a versioned release stream.
60: 10. Check that new links resolve from the file that contains them.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 4. POST-CHECKS
65: 
66: - [ ] Run `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh` against the owning spec folder when the skill change is part of a spec folder.
67: - [ ] Run `python3 .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/scripts/verify_alignment_drift.py --root .skilled/skills/sk-code` for the live parent-hub example; use the same script with the actual target skill root when reviewing another skill.
68: - [ ] For a flat skill, verify the skill frontmatter includes `description`, `allowed-tools`, and `version` when the skill's family uses versions.
69: - [ ] For a parent hub, verify `mode-registry.json` has `modes[]` entries with `workflowMode`, `packetKind`, `backendKind`, `packet`, `packetSkillName`, `toolSurface`, and `advisorRouting`.
70: - [ ] For a parent hub, verify `hub-router.json` resources resolve on disk and the hub-level `graph-metadata.json` is the only graph identity for the skill family.
71: - [ ] grep verification for the live parent-hub example: `rg -n "mode-registry.json|graph-metadata.json|packetKind|advisorRouting|hub-router.json" .skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md .skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json .skilled/skills/sk-code/graph-metadata.json .skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json`.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 5. RELATED RESOURCES
76: 
77: - `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/README.md` (source index for skill structure rules)
78: - `.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-skill/references/parent-skill/parent-skills-nested-packets.md` (parent-hub structure and metadata contract)
79: - Parent-hub example: `.skilled/skills/sk-code/SKILL.md`, `.skilled/skills/sk-code/ROUTER.md` (machine router: intent map, resource map and load tiers), `.skilled/skills/sk-code/graph-metadata.json`, `.skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json`, `.skilled/skills/sk-code/hub-router.json`
80: - Verification recipes: `.skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/assets/checklists/universal-checklist.md`

14: # TypeScript Code Quality Checklist
15: 
16: Quality validation checklist for TypeScript code in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Specific quality checks for TypeScript files. Use alongside the [universal-checklist.md](./universal-checklist.md) for complete validation.
25: 
26: ### Usage
27: 
28: Apply these checks to TypeScript changes after completing the universal checklist, then use the priority levels below to determine which findings block completion.
29: 
30: ### Priority Levels
31: 
32: | Level | Meaning       | Enforcement                        |
33: |-------|---------------|------------------------------------|
34: | P0    | HARD BLOCKER  | Must fix before commit             |
35: | P1    | Required      | Must fix or get explicit approval  |
36: | P2    | Recommended   | Can defer with justification       |
37: 
38: ---
39: 
40: ## 2. P0 - HARD BLOCKERS
41: 
42: These items MUST be fixed before any commit.
43: 
44: ### File Header
45: 
46: ```markdown
47: [ ] File has TypeScript module header identifying the module
48: ```
49: 
50: **Required format**:
51: ```typescript
52: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
53: // MODULE: [Module Name]
54: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
55: ```
56: 
57: ### No `any` in Public API
58: 
59: ```markdown
60: [ ] No `any` type used in exported functions, interfaces, or type aliases
61: ```
62: 
63: **Correct**:
64: ```typescript
65: export function parse(input: unknown): SearchConfig { }
66: export interface SearchOptions { metadata: Record<string, unknown>; }
67: ```
68: 
69: **Wrong**:
70: ```typescript
71: export function parse(input: any): any { }
72: export interface SearchOptions { metadata: any; }
73: ```
74: 
75: **Exception**: Interop with untyped third-party modules requires justification comment:
76: ```typescript
77: // Interop: sqlite-vec has no type definitions
78: // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
79: const sqliteVec = require('sqlite-vec') as any;
80: ```
81: 
82: ### No Commented-Out Code
83: 
84: ```markdown

14: # Config Quality Standards
15: 
16: Quality gates for JSON/JSONC configuration files used by OpenCode system tooling.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Define deterministic configuration quality checks so config updates stay parseable, low-noise, and maintainable across mixed-language workflows.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: Use when implementing, validating, or reviewing JSON/JSONC configuration quality.
29: 
30: ### Scope
31: 
32: - JSON files (`.json`) with no comments.
33: - JSONC files (`.jsonc`) with bounded purposeful comments.
34: - Feature flags, thresholds, ranking constants, and runtime behavior controls.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. P0 - HARD BLOCKERS
39: 
40: ### Syntax and Parse Safety
41: 
42: - JSON/JSONC must parse cleanly.
43: - No duplicate keys.
44: - No trailing commas in strict JSON files.
45: 
46: ### Header and Section Invariant
47: 
48: - JSONC uses numbered ALL-CAPS section headers for major blocks.
49: - Do not convert header style to sentence case or unnumbered variants.
50: - Header style checks are manual/checklist gates (not hard-failed by `verify_alignment_drift.py`).
51: 
52: ### Deterministic Defaults
53: 
54: - Feature flags and fallback values must be explicit.
55: - If default-on behavior is used, opt-out semantics must be documented inline.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 3. P1 - REQUIRED
60: 
61: ### KISS for Config
62: 
63: - Keep keys and nesting minimal for current behavior needs.
64: - Avoid speculative branches for hypothetical future toggles.
65: 
66: ### DRY for Config
67: 
68: - Repeated literals and thresholds should be centralized once and referenced consistently.
69: - Avoid copy-paste constants across sibling sections.
70: 
71: ### SOLID-Aligned Boundary Checks
72: 
73: - **SRP**: each config section should control one behavior domain.
74: - **OCP**: add new behavior through new section entries before editing stable defaults.
75: - **LSP/ISP/DIP**: section consumers should not require special-case type branching due to inconsistent shape.
76: 
77: ### Comment Policy (JSONC Only)
78: 
79: - Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines.
80: - Comments should explain WHY, not WHAT. No narrative comments.
81: - This policy is a P1 manual/checklist gate (not hard-failed by `verify_alignment_drift.py`).
82: 
83: ---
84: 
85: ## 4. P2 - RECOMMENDED
86: 
87: - Add a durable WHY comment for high-impact rules (never a spec-folder-internal id like `REQ-###`; see `../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md` §4).
88: - Keep key ordering stable (`$schema`, core flags, behavior config, advanced settings).
89: - Include value constraints in comments for opaque numbers.
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 5. VERIFICATION
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # JSON and JSONC parse checks
97: python -m json.tool config.json
98: grep -v '^\s*//' config.jsonc | python -m json.tool
99: 
100: # Header and comment policy spot-checks (JSONC, manual review support)
101: rg -n "^// [0-9]+\\. [A-Z0-9 ()/:-]+$" .skilled/skills/sk-code/sk-code-skilled/references/config
102: ```

14: # Config Style Guide
15: 
16: Formatting standards and conventions for JSONC behavior config and strict-JSON machine descriptors in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines consistent styling rules for configuration files to ensure readability and maintainability across OpenCode behavior config and machine descriptor files.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: Use when writing or reviewing JSONC behavior config or strict-JSON machine descriptors.
29: 
30: ### Scope
31: 
32: Applies to two config genres:
33: - **JSONC behavior config** — human-maintained runtime settings such as `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc`. Comments and trailing commas are syntactically allowed; keep comments purposeful and follow the local file's existing comma style.
34: - **Strict-JSON machine descriptors** — no comments and no trailing commas. This includes advisor descriptors (`description.json`), skill-graph identity (`graph-metadata.json`), hub registries (`mode-registry.json`), and the root OpenCode runtime config (`opencode.json`).
35: 
36: ### Key Sources
37: 
38: | File | Evidence |
39: |------|----------|
40: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc` | Header format, section comments, structure |
41: | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/description.json` | Advisor descriptor shape |
42: | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/graph-metadata.json` | Skill-graph identity shape |
43: | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json` | Hub registry shape |
44: | `opencode.json` | Root OpenCode runtime config shape |
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: ## 2. FILE STRUCTURE
49: 
50: Use JSONC structure rules only for JSONC behavior config. Strict-JSON machine descriptors must stay parseable as plain JSON: no comments, no trailing commas, and no header blocks.
51: 
52: ### JSONC Header
53: 
54: Use the standard comment header for JSONC behavior config files:
55: 
56: ```jsonc
57: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
58: // CONFIG: [CONFIG NAME]
59: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
60: {
61:   // Configuration content
62: }
63: ```
64: 
65: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:1-3`
66: 
67: ### Section Organization
68: 
69: Organize JSONC behavior configuration into numbered sections:
70: 
71: ```jsonc
72: {
73:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74:   // 1. LEGACY SETTINGS
75:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
76:   "maxResultPreview": 500,
77:   "maxConversationMessages": 100,
78: 
79:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
80:   // 2. SEMANTIC SEARCH
81:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
82:   "semanticSearch": {
83:     "enabled": true,
84:     "minSimilarityScore": 50
85:   }
86: }
87: ```
88: 
89: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:5-24`
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 3. NAMING CONVENTIONS
94: 
95: ### Property Keys
96: 
97: **Use**: `camelCase` for all property keys
98: 
99: ```jsonc
100: {
101:   // Correct - camelCase
102:   "maxResultPreview": 500,
103:   "minSimilarityScore": 50,
104:   "autoRebuildOnSave": true,
105:   "databasePath": "./database.sqlite",
106: 
107:   // WRONG - other cases
108:   "max_result_preview": 500,    // snake_case
109:   "MaxResultPreview": 500,      // PascalCase
110:   "max-result-preview": 500     // kebab-case
111: }
112: ```
113: 
114: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc` throughout
115: 
116: ### Boolean Properties
117: 
118: Use positive naming (avoid double negatives):
119: 
120: ```jsonc
121: {
122:   // Correct - positive naming
123:   "enabled": true,
124:   "verifyOnStartup": false,
125:   "autoRebuildOnSave": true,
126: 
127:   // WRONG - double negatives
128:   "disableVerification": true,  // Confusing
129:   "noAutoRebuild": false        // Double negative
130: }
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Nested Objects
134: 
135: Use descriptive names for nested configuration sections:
136: 
137: ```jsonc
138: {
139:   "semanticSearch": {
140:     "enabled": true,
141:     "minSimilarityScore": 50,
142:     "maxResults": 10
143:   },
144:   "memoryIndex": {
145:     "databasePath": "./database.sqlite",
146:     "autoRebuildOnSave": true
147:   }
148: }
149: ```
150: 
151: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:19-30`
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: ## 4. COMMENTS (JSONC)
156: 
157: Comments belong only in JSONC behavior config. Strict-JSON machine descriptors (`description.json`, `graph-metadata.json`, `mode-registry.json`, `opencode.json`) cannot contain comments.
158: 
159: ### Section Headers
160: 
161: Use consistent section header format:
162: 
163: ```jsonc
164: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
165: // N. SECTION NAME
166: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
167: ```
168: 
169: The divider line should be 67 characters (same as header width).
170: 
171: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:5-7`
172: 
173: ### Inline Comments
174: 
175: Use inline comments to explain non-obvious values:
176: 
177: 1. **Quantity limit (Skilled surface setting):** Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines in JSONC blocks, this surface's budget for the shared comment-density rule (see [naming and commenting](../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md))
178: 2. **Purposeful semantics only:** Explain WHY, not WHAT
179: 3. **No narrative/mechanical comments** such as "set value" or "loop through"
180: 
181: ```jsonc
182: {
183:   "scaleDays": 90,              // Half-life ~ 62 days with this value
184:   "enabled": true,              // Explicit opt-out avoids implicit defaults
185:   "decayWeight": 0.3,           // Balances recency vs relevance drift
186:   "rrfK": 60                    // Fixed RRF constant for rank fusion
187: }
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Documentation Comments
191: 
192: Add documentation comments for complex settings:
193: 
194: ```jsonc
195: {
196: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
197: // 3. MEMORY DECAY
198: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
199: // Half-life ≈ 62 days with scaleDays=90
200: "memoryDecay": {
201:     "enabled": true,
202:     "scaleDays": 90,
203:     "decayWeight": 0.3
204:   }
205: }
206: ```
207: 
208: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:39-47`
209: 
210: ---
211: 
212: ## 5. VALUE FORMATTING
213: 
214: ### Strings
215: 
216: Use double quotes for all strings:
217: 
218: ```jsonc
219: {
220:   "databasePath": ".skilled/database.sqlite",
221:   "embeddingModel": "voyage-4",
222:   "styleFallback": "minimal"
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Numbers
227: 
228: Use appropriate number types:
229: 
230: ```jsonc
231: {
232:   "maxResults": 10,             // Integer
233:   "minSimilarityScore": 50,     // Integer percentage
234:   "decayWeight": 0.3,           // Float (0-1)
235:   "rrfK": 60                    // Algorithm constant
236: }
237: ```
238: 
239: ### Booleans
240: 
241: Use lowercase `true`/`false`:
242: 
243: ```jsonc

245:   "enabled": true,

14: # Config Style Guide
15: 
16: Formatting standards and conventions for JSONC behavior config and strict-JSON machine descriptors in the OpenCode development environment.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose
23: 
24: Defines consistent styling rules for configuration files to ensure readability and maintainability across OpenCode behavior config and machine descriptor files.
25: 
26: ### When to Use
27: 
28: Use when writing or reviewing JSONC behavior config or strict-JSON machine descriptors.
29: 
30: ### Scope
31: 
32: Applies to two config genres:
33: - **JSONC behavior config** — human-maintained runtime settings such as `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc`. Comments and trailing commas are syntactically allowed; keep comments purposeful and follow the local file's existing comma style.
34: - **Strict-JSON machine descriptors** — no comments and no trailing commas. This includes advisor descriptors (`description.json`), skill-graph identity (`graph-metadata.json`), hub registries (`mode-registry.json`), and the root OpenCode runtime config (`opencode.json`).
35: 
36: ### Key Sources
37: 
38: | File | Evidence |
39: |------|----------|
40: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc` | Header format, section comments, structure |
41: | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/description.json` | Advisor descriptor shape |
42: | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/graph-metadata.json` | Skill-graph identity shape |
43: | `.skilled/skills/sk-code/mode-registry.json` | Hub registry shape |
44: | `opencode.json` | Root OpenCode runtime config shape |
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: ## 2. FILE STRUCTURE
49: 
50: Use JSONC structure rules only for JSONC behavior config. Strict-JSON machine descriptors must stay parseable as plain JSON: no comments, no trailing commas, and no header blocks.
51: 
52: ### JSONC Header
53: 
54: Use the standard comment header for JSONC behavior config files:
55: 
56: ```jsonc
57: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
58: // CONFIG: [CONFIG NAME]
59: // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
60: {
61:   // Configuration content
62: }
63: ```
64: 
65: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:1-3`
66: 
67: ### Section Organization
68: 
69: Organize JSONC behavior configuration into numbered sections:
70: 
71: ```jsonc
72: {
73:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
74:   // 1. LEGACY SETTINGS
75:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
76:   "maxResultPreview": 500,
77:   "maxConversationMessages": 100,
78: 
79:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
80:   // 2. SEMANTIC SEARCH
81:   // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
82:   "semanticSearch": {
83:     "enabled": true,
84:     "minSimilarityScore": 50
85:   }
86: }
87: ```
88: 
89: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:5-24`
90: 
91: ---
92: 
93: ## 3. NAMING CONVENTIONS
94: 
95: ### Property Keys
96: 
97: **Use**: `camelCase` for all property keys
98: 
99: ```jsonc
100: {
101:   // Correct - camelCase
102:   "maxResultPreview": 500,
103:   "minSimilarityScore": 50,
104:   "autoRebuildOnSave": true,
105:   "databasePath": "./database.sqlite",
106: 
107:   // WRONG - other cases
108:   "max_result_preview": 500,    // snake_case
109:   "MaxResultPreview": 500,      // PascalCase
110:   "max-result-preview": 500     // kebab-case
111: }
112: ```
113: 
114: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc` throughout
115: 
116: ### Boolean Properties
117: 
118: Use positive naming (avoid double negatives):
119: 
120: ```jsonc
121: {
122:   // Correct - positive naming
123:   "enabled": true,
124:   "verifyOnStartup": false,
125:   "autoRebuildOnSave": true,
126: 
127:   // WRONG - double negatives
128:   "disableVerification": true,  // Confusing
129:   "noAutoRebuild": false        // Double negative
130: }
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Nested Objects
134: 
135: Use descriptive names for nested configuration sections:
136: 
137: ```jsonc
138: {
139:   "semanticSearch": {
140:     "enabled": true,
141:     "minSimilarityScore": 50,
142:     "maxResults": 10
143:   },
144:   "memoryIndex": {
145:     "databasePath": "./database.sqlite",
146:     "autoRebuildOnSave": true
147:   }
148: }
149: ```
150: 
151: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:19-30`
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: ## 4. COMMENTS (JSONC)
156: 
157: Comments belong only in JSONC behavior config. Strict-JSON machine descriptors (`description.json`, `graph-metadata.json`, `mode-registry.json`, `opencode.json`) cannot contain comments.
158: 
159: ### Section Headers
160: 
161: Use consistent section header format:
162: 
163: ```jsonc
164: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
165: // N. SECTION NAME
166: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
167: ```
168: 
169: The divider line should be 67 characters (same as header width).
170: 
171: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:5-7`
172: 
173: ### Inline Comments
174: 
175: Use inline comments to explain non-obvious values:
176: 
177: 1. **Quantity limit (Skilled surface setting):** Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines in JSONC blocks, this surface's budget for the shared comment-density rule (see [naming and commenting](../shared/universal-patterns/naming-and-commenting.md))
178: 2. **Purposeful semantics only:** Explain WHY, not WHAT
179: 3. **No narrative/mechanical comments** such as "set value" or "loop through"
180: 
181: ```jsonc
182: {
183:   "scaleDays": 90,              // Half-life ~ 62 days with this value
184:   "enabled": true,              // Explicit opt-out avoids implicit defaults
185:   "decayWeight": 0.3,           // Balances recency vs relevance drift
186:   "rrfK": 60                    // Fixed RRF constant for rank fusion
187: }
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Documentation Comments
191: 
192: Add documentation comments for complex settings:
193: 
194: ```jsonc
195: {
196: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
197: // 3. MEMORY DECAY
198: // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
199: // Half-life ≈ 62 days with scaleDays=90
200: "memoryDecay": {
201:     "enabled": true,
202:     "scaleDays": 90,
203:     "decayWeight": 0.3
204:   }
205: }
206: ```
207: 
208: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:39-47`
209: 
210: ---
211: 
212: ## 5. VALUE FORMATTING
213: 
214: ### Strings
215: 
216: Use double quotes for all strings:
217: 
218: ```jsonc
219: {
220:   "databasePath": ".skilled/database.sqlite",
221:   "embeddingModel": "voyage-4",
222:   "styleFallback": "minimal"
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: ### Numbers
227: 
228: Use appropriate number types:
229: 
230: ```jsonc
231: {
232:   "maxResults": 10,             // Integer
233:   "minSimilarityScore": 50,     // Integer percentage
234:   "decayWeight": 0.3,           // Float (0-1)
235:   "rrfK": 60                    // Algorithm constant
236: }
237: ```
238: 
239: ### Booleans
240: 
241: Use lowercase `true`/`false`:
242: 
243: ```jsonc
244: {
245:   "enabled": true,
246:   "verifyOnStartup": false,
247:   "alwaysSurface": true
248: }
249: ```
250: 
251: ### Null Values
252: 
253: Use `null` for explicitly unset values:
254: 
255: ```jsonc
256: {
257:   "autoExpireDays": null,       // No expiration
258:   "maxTokens": null             // No limit
259: }
260: ```
261:

270:   "featureName": {
271:     "enabled": true,
272:     "option1": "value",
273:     "option2": 100
274:   }
275: }
276: ```
277: 
278: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:19-24`
279:

281: 
282: ```jsonc

284:   "importanceTiers": {
285:     "constitutional": { "searchBoost": 3.0, "decay": false },
286:     "critical": { "searchBoost": 2.0, "decay": false },
287:     "important": { "searchBoost": 1.5, "decay": false },
288:     "normal": { "searchBoost": 1.0, "decay": true },
289:     "temporary": { "searchBoost": 0.5, "decay": true }
290:   }
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:53-60`
295: 
296: ### Rule Configuration

300:   "contextTypeDetection": {
301:     "enabled": true,

303:       "research": { "readToolsThreshold": 0.5, "writeToolsMax": 0.1 },

306:     },

308:   }
309: }
310: ```
311: 
312: **Evidence**: `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/config/config.jsonc:76-87`
313:

316: ## 7. SCHEMA REFERENCE
317: 
318: ### Including Schema
319: 
320: Reference JSON Schema when available:
321:

338: }
339: ```
340:

344: 
345: ### Indentation
346: 
347: Use 2 spaces for indentation (consistent with JSON convention):
348: 
349: ```jsonc

351:   "level1": {
352:     "level2": {
353:       "level3": "value"
354:     }
355:   }
356: }

=== minimum-evidence-gate 14-25

This scenario validates the M-2 minimum-evidence gate for `CR-033`. It focuses on a scratch repository with a five-line non-sensitive diff under an exported threshold, the exact skip line that diff produces, and a second run in the same repository where a `*token*` path arrives and the full review must run regardless of line count.

### Why This Matters

M-2 is the gate that trades a full review for a cheaper skip on trivially small diffs, and its whole safety rests on one exception: six high-risk path classes are never skipped. A gate that skips too eagerly hides exactly the defects a review exists to catch, and a gate that never skips is dead weight. The two halves need separate evidence, which is why this scenario runs the same threshold twice: once on a diff that must skip and once on a diff that must not. No other scenario exports the variable, runs the counting command, or asserts the skip line, so without this one the gate could change its threshold semantics, its count, or its taxonomy and the battery would stay green. `SKILL.md` §8.2 holds the contract and `scripts/README.md` holds the whole-output rule the checker enforces.

40: 
41: ### Template Focus
42: 
43: The README gives people a human entry point, current capabilities and a clear route to supporting files. This template provides:
44: 
45: - A one-line pitch in a blockquote right after the H1, stating the outcome before any tool name.

49: - Versioning conventions and a validation checklist that matches the pilot's gates.
50: 
51: ---
52:

54: 
55: A skill README uses numbered ALL-CAPS H2 sections with `---` dividers between them. The default order:
56: 
57: | # | Section | Purpose | Keep When |
58: |---|---------|---------|-----------|
59: | 1 | AT A GLANCE | Four-row table a reader scans in five seconds | Always |
60: | 2 | OVERVIEW | What the skill is and what the reader gets first, then the optional problem narrative | Always (required by the validator) |
61: | 3 | QUICK START | The fastest path to a first result | Skill has commands, scripts or a workflow |
62: | 4 | HOW IT WORKS | The main workflow in prose, with a small Mermaid diagram for multi-step flows | Skill has non-obvious behavior worth explaining |
63: | 5 | INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION | When to use it, plus how it hands off to sibling skills | Readers can confuse it with a neighbor |
64: | 6 | TROUBLESHOOTING | The failure modes operators actually hit | Predictable issues exist |
65: | 7 | FAQ | The two to five questions readers keep asking | High-value answers exist |
66: | 8 | VERIFICATION | How you know the skill works | Skill ships a playbook or validation command |
67: | 9 | RELATED DOCUMENTS | Stable links out, `SKILL.md` first | Always when links exist |

76: ### Capability Section Pattern
77: 
78: When a skill has a headline strength, add a named capability section after What It Does.

80: Use an analogy only when it clarifies the mechanism.
81: Name the section after its domain and add one table row per capability.
82: State the file or data the skill can operate on.

92: ```

97: 
98: - Apply the [Prose Clarity Checklist](../../references/skill/creation-workflow.md#prose-clarity-checklist) to README prose.

107: - Name the canonical command or entry point in OVERVIEW or QUICK START so a reader knows where to start.
108: - Link to real files under `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, `feature-catalog/` or `manual-testing-playbook/`. Verify each path resolves.
109: - State the expected output for every command you show, so a reader can tell success from failure.
110: - Be honest about boundaries and trade-offs. If the skill does not own something, say which skill does.

# Scripts

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

`scripts/` owns the `sk-code-quality` skill's quality runner and its three standalone checkers (comment hygiene, dist staleness and the ceiling-marker report). The runner prints one verdict for a change in any repository and calls the checkers it needs. Each entry point stays thin: `quality-gate.cjs` parses its flags and prints, `check-comment-hygiene.sh` keeps the rule table its callers read out of its text, and the work sits in the modules under `lib/`. The per-edit PostToolUse adapters and their shared dispatch table live in `.skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/`, and the `hooks/` subfolder here keeps only the legacy `claude-posttooluse.sh`.
